short: Soviet forces liberated the Auschwitz concentration camp, uncovering the industrial scale of the Nazi extermination programme.
full:
On 27 January 1945, advancing troops of the Soviet Red Army's 60th Army entered the Auschwitz concentration and extermination camp complex in occupied Poland. They found approximately 7,000 emaciated prisoners who had been left behind because they were deemed too weak to endure the forced 'death marches' initiated by the retreating SS days earlier. The liberators also discovered hundreds of thousands of personal items, including men's suits, women's outfits, and tons of human hair, providing stark evidence of the mass murder that had taken place.

The liberation revealed the unprecedented scale of the Holocaust to the world, confirming reports of industrialised extermination that had previously been met with disbelief. Over 1.1 million people, the vast majority of them Jews, had been murdered at Auschwitz between 1940 and 1945. The date of its liberation is now observed globally as International Holocaust Remembrance Day.
